# Introduction
- Problem: People often feel indecisive or don’t know which leisure activities or hobbies might fit their interests, time, or location.
- Solution: Our app “What’s Today?”
- Users input age, time of day, day of the week, and location to receive general leisure activities and hobbies.
    - ATUS data
- Secondary Component: NYC meetup.com events
  - Join a group, try something new, be spontaneous!
- Interactive dashboard and dynamic tables and visualizations that update immediately with user selections

# Data and Methodology - ATUS
- American Time Use Survey (ATUS)
  - Existing datasets  (US Bureau of Labor Statistics)
  - Measures the amount of time people spend doing various activities
- Methods
  - Merging Resp, Roster, & Activity files
  - Selecting relevant columns, recoding numerical codes to text labels
  - Descriptive statistics (frequency distribution, mean duration, etc.)
    
# Data and Methodology - Meetup.com
- Meetup.com
- Scraped the website
  - Name, Date & time
  - Group/organization
  - Several categories
- Chromote
  - Package for web page interaction
  - Headless Chrome session

# Data and Methodology - Application
- GitHub Repository
  - Allowed for version control and collaboration
- R Shiny
  - Open-source R package
  - Build interactive web applications directly from R
- Global.R
  - Loaded in libraries and data
  - read_csv() and bind_rows()
- UI.R
  - Created visual layout for user input and output
  - selectInput(), plotlyOutput(), DTOutput(), titlePanel()
- Server.R
  - App logic, filtering, and rendering outputs
  - ATUS Data: filtered by user selections
  - Meetup.com Data: Filtered by event category
